newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- ABBEY NATIONAL TO RAISE RATES

Britain's large mortgage lenders are set for their first round of interest rate rises for almost two years when Abbey National confirms on Monday an expected increase of 0.25 percentage points. Another large lender, the Halifax Building Society, has said that if the Abbey raises its rates then it would be likely to have to respond. The moves follow figures last week showing that house prices are increasing by over 8 per cent.
-- PIFCO SETS SIGHTS ON KENWOOD TO TACKLE BIG RIVALS

Household appliances group Pifco is said to be targeting its larger rival Kenwood Appliances in a bid to create a British company large enough to compete on a European scale. A combined company formed from Pifco and Kenwood would have sales approaching 250 million stg. Pifco currently has a market capitalization of 48 million stg, about half the size of Kenwood. Kenwood has confirmed that an informal approach has been received from Pifco.
-- NATWEST LOOKS AT DIVERSIFYING INTO STATIONERY MARKET

High street banking group National Westminster is reported to be considering diversifying outside financial services for the first time, in a venture selling office supplies. The plan, in which NatWest would supply stationery items to its business customers and other companies, has been attacked by the stationery trade and suppliers who are also NatWest customers. They have threatened to switch their accounts to other banks should NatWest proceed with the plans.
-- EU AGREES RULES FOR GENETICALLY ENGINEERED FOODS

Environmental campaigners have blasted a decision by the European Union to allow genetically-engineered food to be sold without special labelling. The Union has been debating the controversial measure for months, with countries such as Germany and Austria backing the calls of environmentalists for tough rules on the grounds that genetically-engineered food may be harmful to humans. Under the EU rules, products which could theoretically grow if put in soil ('live' goods) will have to be labelled if they are genetically modified, but 'novel' foods (those which have never been sold in the EU before) can be sold without special labels.
-- BANKS BACK PLAN FOR RESCUING BIG COMPANIES

A survey from accountants Price Waterhouse has revealed that 74 per cent of the bankers it consulted would support an initiative to reform the mechanism by which lenders co-operate to try to save big companies which run into financial trouble. 53 per cent of those surveyed also backed the appointment of independent 'ringmasters' to mediate between different stakeholder groups in troubled companies.
-- EUROTUNNEL SEEKS GO-AHEAD AFTER TESTS

Eurotunnel, the operators of the Channel Tunnel, has carried out a test evacuation involving 500 'passengers' trapped on a train in the second, undamaged, tunnel. The exercise was intended to prove to the safety authority that it is safe to resume services through the tunnel. Repairs to the damaged section of the tunnel are expected to take five months, but Eurotunnel and train operators Eurostar say they could reinstate more than 90 per cent of passengers services within a very short time once safety clearance is given.
-- INNTREPRENEUR WINS BACKING ON PLEDGE

The Office of Fair Trading (OFT) is set to allow Inntrepreneur, the public house company, to go back on a pledge made to competition authorities in 1991 and continue as the sole seller of beer to its pubs after 1998. The pledge was a condition set by the OFT when Inntrepreneur, which is owned by Grand Metropolitan and Foster's Brewing Group, was formed. Inntrepreneur had threatened to sell all or some of its 2,900 pub chain should the undertaking not be lifted.
-- HALIFAX AIMS TO AVERT ISSUE CHAOS

Halifax Building Society is preparing for next year's 10 billion stg flotation by encouraging the 9 million savers and borrowers who are due free shares to place them in a nominee company rather than opt for individual share certificates. The move is designed to reduce the chances of chaos on the first day of trading in what will be the UK's largest single extension of share ownership.
-- EdF AND RWE BUY 240 MILLION STG STAKE IN MOTOR-COLUMBUS

French state-owned utility Electricite de France has joined with German utility RWE Energie to take a 40 per cent stake in Swiss electricity company Motor-Columbus. The 240 million stg deal was announced shortly after Swiss industrial conglomerate Elektrowatt revealed plans to spin off its stakes in four Swiss electric utilities into a new venture named Watt, which will be quoted on the Swiss stock exchange. The two largest shareholders in Motor-Columbus and Elektrowatt - Union Bank of Switzerland and Credit Suisse respectively - had been involved in talks about creating a giant Swiss electricity utility, but the negotiations broke down.
-- RUSSIAN UTILITY TO LAUNCH EUROBOND NEXT YEAR

Russian utilities giant Unified Energy Systems (UES) is joining the rush by Russian companies and regional authorities towards the global money markets with plans for a eurobond issue next year. The announcement of the plans follows a surprise move by the Russian government last week to cancel a UES convertible bond issue which the company had hoped would raise about $350 million. Instead, the government has decided to sell an 8.5 per cent stake in UES in a cash auction which is expected to raise about $300 million for the Russian treasury.
